Schematic illustration of the advantages of using PEDOT:PSS/PEG (PPP) with SWCNTs as a bifunctional binder for LFP cathodes, which highlights the enhanced energy density (99 % LFP loading) and improved electrode performance enabled by PEG-induced phase separation and conductive networks of SWCNTs. 2.2. Morphological and interfacial characteristics of LFP cathodes with PEDOT:PSS/PEG binder Although the 4 % PEDOT:PSS/PEG binder ensures uniform coverage and effectively enhances electron conductivity and charge transport, the use of minimal binder content raises a reasonable concern that cohesion properties could weaken, potentially compromising the battery perfor­ mance. To address this issue, we evaluated the cohesion characteristics using a surface and interfacial cutting and analysis system (SAICAS) [61].
